newsitem.title: UK: Rouse ends clearing agreement with IPE local trade.
newsitem.headline: Rouse ends clearing agreement with IPE local trade.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Rouse terminated its clearing agreement with an independent trader on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) this week after he exceeded his trading position limits, industry sources said.
The industry sources said the trader, known as a "local" who operated on his own account, had a 40 contract limit with Rouse but had oversold that position by as much as 1,300 lots.

Rouse referred all queries on the matter to its chairman Roy Leighton who was out of the office on Friday. IPE vice president of business development, Richard Ward, said Rouse had informed the IPE of its decision to terminate its clearing agreement with the trader.
"Credit Lyonnais Rouse has terminated its clearing agreement with (the trader). He is prohibited from trading on the IPE until he sets up a new clearing agreement," Ward said.
IPE traders said the local trader may have run up obligations of more than $500,000 which his clearing broker would be liable for with the London Clearing House.
The IPE's Ward would not comment on how much the trader could owe Rouse but he said the company would be obligated to clear the matter with the LCH.
